candidates.current_role: Montgomery County Judge since January 2019
candidates.background: Mark Keough has been Montgomery County Judge since January 1, 2019. He previously represented District 15 in the Texas House for two terms (84th and 85th Legislatures). Before public office he worked as an automotive dealer principal and general manager and as a minister.

priorities.text: Lists a modern jail, a new courthouse and expanded roads as his top priorities, calling them "vital investments in our safety and economy."
Pledges to keep taxes low and says tax dollars should go to "needs, not waste."
Says county facility needs should be addressed "in pieces, being fiscally responsible and not constantly increasing taxes."
Says he will manage growth without "turning into Harris County."

record.text: Cites a roughly 20 percent tax reduction and full funding for law enforcement during his tenure, according to his own Q&A answers.
Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 51 percent of the vote over Wayne Mack, a margin of 1,519 votes.

notes.text: First won the county judge seat in 2018 and won renomination in 2022 with 66.11 percent of the Republican primary vote.

q_county_tax.summary: Says he will keep fighting for low taxes and favors phasing in jail, courthouse and other projects rather than constantly raising taxes.

issue_notes.summary: Says growth may allow the county to keep passing road bonds every three to four years because infrastructure must expand.

candidates.background: Brian Cantrell is the Waller County fire marshal and chief of emergency management and homeland security. priorities.text: Lists managing growth and infrastructure, public safety, supporting county employees, transparency, local hiring and parks as his six priorities.

promises.text: Proposes a road and drainage needs assessment, a centralized emergency operations center, published budget summaries, digital permits and forms, and Precinct 4's first park.

notes.text: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 785 votes (51 percent) over former Katy council member Dan Smith.
The seat is open because Commissioner Justin Beckendorff ran for county judge.
